title: distinguish average speed (path length) from average velocity (signed displacement) when the motion reverses direction
stem: A runner on a straight track uses an x-axis pointing east. She starts at x = +3 m, runs to x = +11 m in 4 s, then reverses and runs to x = −1 m in another 6 s. For the whole 10 s, which choice gives her average speed and average velocity?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Average speed 2.0 m/s; average velocity +0.4 m/s.
choices.rationale: Average velocity has the same sign as the net displacement, which is −4 m on this axis, so its sign is −. Reversing it describes the opposite displacement.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Average speed 2.0 m/s; average velocity −0.4 m/s.
choices.rationale: Correct: Displacement = −4 m, path length = 20 m, time = 10 s. Speed = 20/10 = 2.0 m/s; velocity = −4/10 = −0.4 m/s.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Average speed 0.4 m/s; average velocity −0.4 m/s.
choices.rationale: Average speed is total path length divided by time, 20 m over 10 s. Using the 4 m net displacement drops the back-and-forth part of the path.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Average speed 2.0 m/s; average velocity +2.0 m/s.
choices.rationale: Average velocity uses the net displacement of −4 m, not the 20 m path length. Speed and velocity agree only when the motion never reverses.

title: distinguish average speed (path length) from average velocity (signed displacement) when the motion reverses direction (variant 1)
stem: A cart on a straight track starts at x = −5 m, rolls to x = +7 m in 3 s, then reverses and rolls to x = +1 m in the next 3 s. Using the track's x-axis, which choice gives the cart's average speed and average velocity over the full 6 s?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Average speed 3.0 m/s; average velocity −1.0 m/s.
choices.rationale: Average velocity has the same sign as the net displacement, which is +6 m on this axis, so its sign is +. Reversing it describes the opposite displacement.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Average speed 3.0 m/s; average velocity +1.0 m/s.
choices.rationale: Correct: Displacement = +6 m, path length = 18 m, time = 6 s. Speed = 18/6 = 3.0 m/s; velocity = +6/6 = +1.0 m/s.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Average speed 1.0 m/s; average velocity +1.0 m/s.
choices.rationale: Average speed is total path length divided by time, 18 m over 6 s. Using the 6 m net displacement drops the back-and-forth part of the path.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Average speed 3.0 m/s; average velocity +3.0 m/s.
choices.rationale: Average velocity uses the net displacement of +6 m, not the 18 m path length. Speed and velocity agree only when the motion never reverses.

title: distinguish average speed (path length) from average velocity (signed displacement) when the motion reverses direction (variant 2)
stem: An elevator car is described with a y-axis pointing up. It starts at y = +20 m, descends to y = 0 m in 8 s, then rises to y = +8 m in the next 2 s. Which choice gives its average speed and average velocity over the 10 s?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Average speed 2.8 m/s; average velocity −1.2 m/s.
choices.rationale: Correct: Displacement = −12 m, path length = 28 m, time = 10 s. Speed = 28/10 = 2.8 m/s; velocity = −12/10 = −1.2 m/s.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Average speed 2.8 m/s; average velocity +1.2 m/s.
choices.rationale: Average velocity has the same sign as the net displacement, which is −12 m on this axis, so its sign is −. Reversing it describes the opposite displacement.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Average speed 1.2 m/s; average velocity −1.2 m/s.
choices.rationale: Average speed is total path length divided by time, 28 m over 10 s. Using the 12 m net displacement drops the back-and-forth part of the path.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Average speed 2.8 m/s; average velocity +2.8 m/s.
choices.rationale: Average velocity uses the net displacement of −12 m, not the 28 m path length. Speed and velocity agree only when the motion never reverses.

title: distinguish average speed (path length) from average velocity (signed displacement) when the motion reverses direction (variant 3)
stem: A ball rolls along a straight groove with an x-axis pointing right. It starts at x = +4 m, reaches x = −6 m after 5 s, then turns and reaches x = −2 m after another 5 s. Which choice gives its average speed and average velocity for the 10 s?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Average speed 1.4 m/s; average velocity +0.6 m/s.
choices.rationale: Average velocity has the same sign as the net displacement, which is −6 m on this axis, so its sign is −. Reversing it describes the opposite displacement.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Average speed 0.6 m/s; average velocity −0.6 m/s.
choices.rationale: Average speed is total path length divided by time, 14 m over 10 s. Using the 6 m net displacement drops the back-and-forth part of the path.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Average speed 1.4 m/s; average velocity −0.6 m/s.
choices.rationale: Correct: Displacement = −6 m, path length = 14 m, time = 10 s. Speed = 14/10 = 1.4 m/s; velocity = −6/10 = −0.6 m/s.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Average speed 1.4 m/s; average velocity +1.4 m/s.
choices.rationale: Average velocity uses the net displacement of −6 m, not the 14 m path length. Speed and velocity agree only when the motion never reverses.

title: predict how reversing the axis direction or origin changes signed quantities (position, displacement, velocity, accelera
stem: A ball is tossed straight up from a hand, rises to its highest point, and is caught back at the same height. A student first describes the rise from release to the peak with upward as the positive direction, then describes the same rise with downward as the positive direction and the same origin. Which statement correctly compares the two descriptions?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Displacement and average velocity for the rise change sign, while distance traveled and average speed keep their values.
choices.rationale: Correct: Reversing the axis flips the sign of every vector component, so displacement and average velocity change sign. Path length and speed are magnitudes, so they do not change.

choices.label: B
choices.text: All four quantities change sign, because the axis direction was reversed.
choices.rationale: Distance traveled and average speed are magnitudes built from path length, so they have no sign to flip. Only the vector quantities depend on which way the axis points.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Displacement changes sign, but average velocity keeps its sign because the ball's motion is unchanged.
choices.rationale: Average velocity is displacement divided by a positive time interval, so it must take the sign of the displacement. If one flips, the other flips.

choices.label: D
choices.text: No quantity changes, since the ball's physical motion is identical in both descriptions.
choices.rationale: The motion is the same, but the numerical value of a vector component depends on the axis direction. Reversing the axis reverses the signs of displacement and velocity.

title: predict how reversing the axis direction or origin changes signed quantities (position, displacement, velocity, accelera (variant 1)
stem: A cart rolling to the right slows steadily and comes to rest. One student takes right as positive and another takes left as positive. Which statement about their descriptions of the slowing-down interval is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Both students record a negative acceleration, because slowing down always means negative acceleration.
choices.rationale: The sign of acceleration depends on the axis direction. For the student with left positive, the cart's velocity change points left, so the acceleration is positive.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Velocity and acceleration both flip sign, so for the second student the cart is speeding up.
choices.rationale: When both flip, they still have opposite signs relative to each other. Opposite signs of velocity and acceleration mean slowing down in either description.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The two students' velocities have opposite signs and their accelerations have opposite signs, yet both agree the cart is slowing down.
choices.rationale: Correct: Right-positive: v > 0 and a < 0. Left-positive: v < 0 and a > 0. Opposite signs of v and a mean slowing down in both.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Only the acceleration flips sign; the velocity is positive for both students because the cart moves forward.
choices.rationale: Velocity is a vector whose sign depends on the chosen axis, so the left-positive student records the cart's velocity as negative.

title: predict how reversing the axis direction or origin changes signed quantities (position, displacement, velocity, accelera (variant 2)
stem: A drone hovers 10 m above the ground and rises to 25 m above the ground. Student P measures position upward from the ground. Student Q places the origin on a roof 40 m above the ground and takes downward as positive. Which choice gives Student Q's initial position, final position, and displacement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Initial +30 m, final +15 m, displacement +15 m, because the drone still climbs 15 m.
choices.rationale: The displacement is the final position minus the initial position, which is 15 − 30 = −15 m on a downward-positive axis. Climbing is motion in the negative direction here.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Initial −30 m, final −15 m, displacement +15 m, because the drone is below the origin.
choices.rationale: With downward as positive, a point below the origin has a positive coordinate. Calling it negative ignores the axis direction Student Q chose.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Initial +30 m, final +15 m, displacement −15 m.
choices.rationale: Correct: Roof origin, down positive: initial = 40 − 10 = +30 m, final = 40 − 25 = +15 m, displacement = 15 − 30 = −15 m.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Initial +10 m, final +25 m, displacement −15 m, because positions do not depend on the origin.
choices.rationale: Positions are measured from the chosen origin, so they differ between students. Only the displacement magnitude of 15 m is shared.

title: predict how reversing the axis direction or origin changes signed quantities (position, displacement, velocity, accelera (variant 3)
stem: A bird leaves a perch, flies 6.0 m north along a straight line, then flies 6.0 m south back to the perch, taking 4.0 s in all. Student M takes north as positive and Student N takes south as positive. Which statement about the round trip is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Student M finds an average velocity of +3.0 m/s and Student N finds −3.0 m/s.
choices.rationale: The bird ends where it started, so the displacement is zero for both students. A nonzero average velocity would require a net change in position.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Both students find an average velocity of 3.0 m/s, since the speed is the same for them.
choices.rationale: Average speed uses the 12 m path length, but average velocity uses the net displacement, which is zero. The two quantities are not interchangeable.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Both students find zero average velocity and zero average speed, because the bird returns to the perch.
choices.rationale: Returning to the start makes displacement zero, not distance. The bird flew 12 m in 4.0 s, so its average speed is 3.0 m/s.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Both students find zero displacement and zero average velocity, and both find an average speed of 3.0 m/s.
choices.rationale: Correct: Net displacement is 0, so average velocity is 0 for either axis. Path length is 12 m, so average speed = 12/4.0 = 3.0 m/s.

title: use the relative signs of velocity and acceleration to decide speeding up or slowing down, then apply v = v0 + at throug
stem: A cart moves along a straight track with the positive axis pointing right. At t = 0 its velocity is −3 m/s and its acceleration is a constant −2 m/s². Which choice correctly describes the cart at t = 0 and gives its velocity at t = 2.0 s?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Moving left and slowing down; v = +1 m/s.
choices.rationale: A negative acceleration does not by itself mean slowing down. Velocity and acceleration here share the same sign, so the speed grows rather than shrinks.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Moving left and speeding up; v = +7 m/s.
choices.rationale: Speeding up to a speed of 7 m/s leftward still gives a negative velocity on this axis. The positive sign would mean the cart is moving right.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Moving left and speeding up; v = −7 m/s.
choices.rationale: Correct: v = v0 + at = −3 + (−2)(2.0) = -7 m/s. Velocity and acceleration have the same sign, so the speed increases.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Moving left and speeding up; v = −5 m/s.
choices.rationale: The velocity change is a·t = (−2)(2.0) = −4 m/s, the full interval. Using only half the time reaches −5 m/s, which is not the velocity at 2.0 s.

title: use the relative signs of velocity and acceleration to decide speeding up or slowing down, then apply v = v0 + at throug (variant 1)
stem: A cart moves along a straight track with the positive axis pointing right. At t = 0 its velocity is +4 m/s and its acceleration is a constant −2 m/s². Which choice correctly describes the cart at t = 0 and gives its velocity at t = 3.0 s?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Moving right and speeding up; v = +10 m/s.
choices.rationale: Velocity and acceleration have opposite signs here, so the cart loses speed at first. Adding the magnitude of the acceleration treats it as always speeding the cart up.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Moving right and slowing down; v = 0 m/s.
choices.rationale: The velocity does reach zero, at t = 2.0 s, but the constant acceleration continues to act. By 3.0 s the cart has reversed and moves left at 2 m/s.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Moving left and speeding up; v = −2 m/s.
choices.rationale: The direction of motion at t = 0 comes from the sign of the velocity, which is positive, so the cart starts out moving right. The acceleration's sign does not set that direction.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Moving right and slowing down; v = −2 m/s.
choices.rationale: Correct: v = 4 + (−2)(3.0) = -2 m/s. At t = 0, v > 0 and a < 0, so the cart is slowing; it stops at t = 2.0 s and reverses.

title: use the relative signs of velocity and acceleration to decide speeding up or slowing down, then apply v = v0 + at throug (variant 2)
stem: A cart moves along a straight track with the positive axis pointing right. At t = 0 its velocity is −5 m/s and its acceleration is a constant +2 m/s². Which choice correctly describes the cart at t = 0 and gives its velocity at t = 4.0 s?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Moving left and speeding up; v = −13 m/s.
choices.rationale: The positive acceleration points opposite to the leftward velocity, so it reduces the speed. Treating a positive acceleration as adding to a leftward speed gets the relationship backward.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Moving left and slowing down; v = 0 m/s.
choices.rationale: The cart does stop at t = 2.5 s, but the acceleration keeps acting. After a further 1.5 s it is moving right at 3 m/s.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Moving right and speeding up; v = +13 m/s.
choices.rationale: At t = 0 the velocity is negative, so the cart is moving left. The positive acceleration does not make it start out moving right.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Moving left and slowing down; v = +3 m/s.
choices.rationale: Correct: v = −5 + (2)(4.0) = +3 m/s. Velocity and acceleration start with opposite signs, so the cart slows, stops at 2.5 s, then moves right.

title: use the relative signs of velocity and acceleration to decide speeding up or slowing down, then apply v = v0 + at throug (variant 3)
stem: A cart moves along a straight track with the positive axis pointing right. At t = 0 its velocity is +2 m/s and its acceleration is a constant +3 m/s². Which choice correctly describes the cart at t = 0 and gives its velocity at t = 2.0 s?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Moving right and speeding up; v = +5 m/s.
choices.rationale: The change in velocity is the acceleration multiplied by the time, (3)(2.0) = 6 m/s. Adding the acceleration value directly to 2 m/s leaves out the time factor.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Moving right and speeding up; v = +6 m/s.
choices.rationale: The acceleration only supplies the change in velocity, 6 m/s. The cart's initial 2 m/s must be added, giving 8 m/s.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Moving left and speeding up; v = −8 m/s.
choices.rationale: The positive velocity at t = 0 means the cart moves right. Speeding up in the positive direction gives +8 m/s, not −8 m/s.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Moving right and speeding up; v = +8 m/s.
choices.rationale: Correct: v = 2 + (3)(2.0) = 8 m/s. Both signs are positive, so the speed increases.

title: separate displacement from distance traveled for constant-acceleration motion that reverses at a turning point
stem: A cart on a straight track has an initial velocity of +8.0 m/s and a constant acceleration of −2.0 m/s². Considering the first 6.0 s of motion, which choice gives its displacement and the total distance it travels?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Displacement +12.0 m; distance traveled 20.0 m.
choices.rationale: Correct: Turning point at t = −v0/a = 4.0 s, reached after 16.0 m. x(t) = v0 t + ½ a t² = +12.0 m. Path length = 16.0 + 4.0 = 20.0 m.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Displacement +12.0 m; distance traveled 12.0 m.
choices.rationale: The object reverses at t = 4.0 s, so the path length is greater than the 12.0 m magnitude of the displacement. The two are equal only when the motion never reverses.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Displacement +20.0 m; distance traveled 12.0 m.
choices.rationale: Displacement is the signed change in position from the formula x = v0 t + ½ a t², which gives +12.0 m. The path length of 20.0 m is a different, unsigned quantity.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Displacement +16.0 m; distance traveled 16.0 m.
choices.rationale: The object reverses at t = 4.0 s, but the motion continues until t = 6.0 s. Stopping the calculation at the turning point ignores the return trip.

title: separate displacement from distance traveled for constant-acceleration motion that reverses at a turning point (variant 1)
stem: A ball is thrown straight up at 12 m/s with the upward direction positive and a constant acceleration of −10 m/s². Neglecting air resistance, which choice gives its displacement and the total distance it travels during the first 2.0 s?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Displacement +4.0 m; distance traveled 4.0 m.
choices.rationale: The object reverses at t = 1.2 s, so the path length is greater than the 4.0 m magnitude of the displacement. The two are equal only when the motion never reverses.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Displacement +10.4 m; distance traveled 4.0 m.
choices.rationale: Displacement is the signed change in position from the formula x = v0 t + ½ a t², which gives +4.0 m. The path length of 10.4 m is a different, unsigned quantity.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Displacement +7.2 m; distance traveled 7.2 m.
choices.rationale: The object reverses at t = 1.2 s, but the motion continues until t = 2.0 s. Stopping the calculation at the turning point ignores the return trip.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Displacement +4.0 m; distance traveled 10.4 m.
choices.rationale: Correct: Turning point at t = −v0/a = 1.2 s, reached after 7.2 m. x(t) = v0 t + ½ a t² = +4.0 m. Path length = 7.2 + 3.2 = 10.4 m.

title: separate displacement from distance traveled for constant-acceleration motion that reverses at a turning point (variant 2)
stem: A cart moving along a track at +10 m/s has a constant acceleration of −4.0 m/s². Over the first 5.0 s, which choice gives its displacement and the total distance it travels?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Displacement 0.0 m; distance traveled 0.0 m.
choices.rationale: The object reverses at t = 2.5 s, so the path length is greater than the 0.0 m magnitude of the displacement. The two are equal only when the motion never reverses.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Displacement +25.0 m; distance traveled 25.0 m.
choices.rationale: Displacement is the signed change in position from the formula x = v0 t + ½ a t², which gives 0.0 m. The path length of 25.0 m is a different, unsigned quantity.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Displacement 0.0 m; distance traveled 25.0 m.
choices.rationale: Correct: Turning point at t = −v0/a = 2.5 s, reached after 12.5 m. x(t) = v0 t + ½ a t² = 0.0 m. Path length = 12.5 + 12.5 = 25.0 m.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Displacement +12.5 m; distance traveled 12.5 m.
choices.rationale: The object reverses at t = 2.5 s, but the motion continues until t = 5.0 s. Stopping the calculation at the turning point ignores the return trip.

title: separate displacement from distance traveled for constant-acceleration motion that reverses at a turning point (variant 3)
stem: A sled slides on a slope where the downhill direction is positive. It starts at −9.0 m/s (moving uphill) with a constant acceleration of +3.0 m/s². Over the first 4.0 s, which choice gives its displacement and the total distance it travels?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Displacement −12.0 m; distance traveled 15.0 m.
choices.rationale: Correct: Turning point at t = −v0/a = 3.0 s, reached after 13.5 m. x(t) = v0 t + ½ a t² = −12.0 m. Path length = 13.5 + 1.5 = 15.0 m.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Displacement −12.0 m; distance traveled 12.0 m.
choices.rationale: The object reverses at t = 3.0 s, so the path length is greater than the 12.0 m magnitude of the displacement. The two are equal only when the motion never reverses.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Displacement +15.0 m; distance traveled 12.0 m.
choices.rationale: Displacement is the signed change in position from the formula x = v0 t + ½ a t², which gives −12.0 m. The path length of 15.0 m is a different, unsigned quantity.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Displacement −13.5 m; distance traveled 13.5 m.
choices.rationale: The object reverses at t = 3.0 s, but the motion continues until t = 4.0 s. Stopping the calculation at the turning point ignores the return trip.

title: read position from the signed area under a velocity-time graph, distinguishing zero velocity and a turning point from ze
stem: A cart moves along a straight track. Its velocity–time graph is a single straight line that starts at +6.0 m/s at t = 0 and falls steadily to −6.0 m/s at t = 6.0 s. Take the position at t = 0 as the starting position. Which statement about the cart's position is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is farthest from its start at t = 6 s, because the velocity has its largest negative value there.
choices.rationale: Position depends on the accumulated area under the graph, not on the current value of the velocity. After the crossing, the object moves back toward its start.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is farthest from its start at t = 3 s, 9 m away on the positive side; at t = 6 s it is back at its starting position.
choices.rationale: Correct: Zero crossing at t = 3 s; area = 9 m. Remaining area has magnitude 9 m in the opposite direction, so x(6) = 0 m.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The object is at its starting position at t = 3 s, because the velocity is zero there.
choices.rationale: Zero velocity is not zero position. The velocity is zero at the crossing, while the object has already covered the whole area before it.

choices.label: D
choices.text: At t = 6 s the object is 18 m from its start, because the two areas add.
choices.rationale: The area below the time axis is displacement in the opposite direction, so it subtracts from the area above. The total of the two areas is the path length, not the net displacement.

title: read position from the signed area under a velocity-time graph, distinguishing zero velocity and a turning point from ze (variant 1)
stem: A cart moves along a straight track. Its velocity–time graph is one straight line from +8.0 m/s at t = 0 down to −4.0 m/s at t = 6.0 s. Taking its position at t = 0 as the start, which statement about the cart's position is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is farthest from its start at t = 6 s, because the velocity has its largest negative value there.
choices.rationale: Position depends on the accumulated area under the graph, not on the current value of the velocity. After the crossing, the object moves back toward its start.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The object is at its starting position at t = 4 s, because the velocity is zero there.
choices.rationale: Zero velocity is not zero position. The velocity is zero at the crossing, while the object has already covered the whole area before it.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is farthest from its start at t = 4 s, 16 m away on the positive side; at t = 6 s it is 12 m from its start, on the positive side.
choices.rationale: Correct: Zero crossing at t = 4 s; area = 16 m. Remaining area has magnitude 4 m in the opposite direction, so x(6) = +12 m.

choices.label: D
choices.text: At t = 6 s the object is 20 m from its start, because the two areas add.
choices.rationale: The area below the time axis is displacement in the opposite direction, so it subtracts from the area above. The total of the two areas is the path length, not the net displacement.

title: read position from the signed area under a velocity-time graph, distinguishing zero velocity and a turning point from ze (variant 2)
stem: A robot moves along a straight hallway. Its velocity–time graph is one straight line from −4.0 m/s at t = 0 up to +12 m/s at t = 8.0 s. Taking its position at t = 0 as the start, which statement about the robot's position is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is farthest from its start at t = 2 s, 4 m away, because the velocity is zero there.
choices.rationale: A velocity of zero marks a turning point, not the farthest distance. After the crossing the object moves the other way and keeps going, ending up farther from the start.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is farthest from its start at t = 8 s, 32 m away on the positive side.
choices.rationale: Correct: Zero crossing at t = 2 s; signed area before it = -4 m. Signed area from 2 s to 8 s = +36 m, so x(8) = +32 m. The magnitude is larger at t = 8 s.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is farthest from its start at t = 8 s, 32 m away on the negative side.
choices.rationale: The signed area after the crossing decides the side of the start where the object ends up. The graph shows the object is on the other side.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is farthest from its start at t = 8 s, 40 m away.
choices.rationale: Areas on opposite sides of the time axis subtract. The net position is -4 + (+36) = +32 m, so the object is 32 m away, not 40 m.

title: read position from the signed area under a velocity-time graph, distinguishing zero velocity and a turning point from ze (variant 3)
stem: A sled moves along a straight slope. Its velocity–time graph is one straight line from +5.0 m/s at t = 0 down to −15 m/s at t = 8.0 s. Taking its position at t = 0 as the start, which statement about the sled's position is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is farthest from its start at t = 8 s, 40 m away on the negative side.
choices.rationale: Correct: Zero crossing at t = 2 s; signed area before it = +5 m. Signed area from 2 s to 8 s = -45 m, so x(8) = -40 m. The magnitude is larger at t = 8 s.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is farthest from its start at t = 2 s, 5 m away, because the velocity is zero there.
choices.rationale: A velocity of zero marks a turning point, not the farthest distance. After the crossing the object moves the other way and keeps going, ending up farther from the start.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is farthest from its start at t = 8 s, 40 m away on the positive side.
choices.rationale: The signed area after the crossing decides the side of the start where the object ends up. The graph shows the object is on the other side.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is farthest from its start at t = 8 s, 50 m away.
choices.rationale: Areas on opposite sides of the time axis subtract. The net position is +5 + (-45) = -40 m, so the object is 40 m away, not 50 m.

title: compare slopes (instantaneous versus average velocity) of straight and curved position-time graphs
stem: On one set of axes, the position–time graph of object A is a straight line from the origin to x = 12 m at t = 6.0 s. The graph of object B is a parabola that starts at the origin with zero slope, curves upward, and also reaches x = 12 m at t = 6.0 s. Which statement is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The curved object has the larger average velocity, because it is moving fastest at the end.
choices.rationale: Average velocity is displacement divided by time, and both objects cover the same displacement in the same time. A larger final slope does not change that average.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Both have an average velocity of 2.0 m/s, and their instantaneous velocities are equal at t = 3.0 s.
choices.rationale: Correct: x = bt² with b = 12/6² gives v = 2bt. Setting 2bt equal to the line's slope 2.0 m/s gives t = 3.0 s.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The two objects have the same velocity at every instant, because they start and end at the same positions.
choices.rationale: Same endpoints guarantee the same average velocity only. The curved graph has a changing slope, while the straight line has a constant slope.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The two objects have equal instantaneous velocities only at t = 6.0 s, where the graphs meet.
choices.rationale: Meeting at a point means equal positions, not equal slopes. At that point the curve is steeper than the line, so the velocities differ.

title: combine and subtract signed velocities in one dimension across two or three reference frames
stem: On a straight east–west road, car P travels east at 20 m/s and truck T travels east at 14 m/s, both measured relative to the ground. A motorcycle M travels west at 10 m/s relative to the ground. Which choice gives M's velocity relative to P and T's velocity relative to P?

choices.label: A
choices.text: M relative to P: 30 m/s west; T relative to P: 6 m/s west.
choices.rationale: Correct: East positive: v_M/P = −10 − 20 = −30 m/s; v_T/P = 14 − 20 = −6 m/s.

choices.label: B
choices.text: M relative to P: 10 m/s west; T relative to P: 6 m/s west.
choices.rationale: The motorcycle's 10 m/s is measured relative to the ground, not to car P. P is itself moving east at 20 m/s, so the relative speed is larger.

choices.label: C
choices.text: M relative to P: 30 m/s west; T relative to P: 6 m/s east.
choices.rationale: T moves east slower than P, so from P's viewpoint T falls behind, toward the west. The relative velocity is v_T − v_P = −6 m/s, which points west.

choices.label: D
choices.text: M relative to P: 30 m/s west; T relative to P: 34 m/s west.
choices.rationale: Both vehicles in the second case move east, so their velocities subtract. Adding the 14 m/s and 20 m/s is correct only for objects moving in opposite directions.

title: combine and subtract signed velocities in one dimension across two or three reference frames (variant 1)
stem: A train moves east at 25 m/s relative to the ground. A passenger walks toward the front of the train at 2.0 m/s relative to the train. A second train on a parallel track moves west at 15 m/s relative to the ground. Which choice gives the passenger's velocity relative to the ground and relative to the second train?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ground: 23 m/s east; second train: 38 m/s east.
choices.rationale: Walking toward the front adds to the train's velocity, since both point east. Subtracting 2.0 m/s treats the walk as toward the rear.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ground: 27 m/s east; second train: 12 m/s east.
choices.rationale: The second train moves west, opposite to the passenger. Relative to it, the passenger's velocity is 27 − (−15), so the speeds add instead of subtract.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ground: 25 m/s east; second train: 40 m/s east.
choices.rationale: The passenger's walking speed relative to the train must be included. It adds to the 25 m/s, giving 27 m/s relative to the ground.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ground: 27 m/s east; second train: 42 m/s east.
choices.rationale: Correct: East positive: v_p/ground = 25 + 2.0 = +27 m/s. v_p/second = 27 − (−15) = +42 m/s.

title: combine and subtract signed velocities in one dimension across two or three reference frames (variant 2)
stem: A moving walkway carries people east at 1.5 m/s relative to the floor. A person walks west on the walkway at 2.0 m/s relative to the walkway. A runner on the floor beside it moves east at 3.0 m/s relative to the floor. Which choice gives the person's velocity relative to the floor and the runner's velocity relative to the person?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Person: 3.5 m/s west; runner relative to person: 6.5 m/s east.
choices.rationale: The walkway carries the person east, which partly cancels the westward walk. The two velocities have opposite directions, so they subtract rather than add.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Person: 0.5 m/s west; runner relative to person: 2.5 m/s east.
choices.rationale: The runner moves east and the person moves west, so their relative velocity is 3.0 − (−0.5) = 3.5 m/s. Subtracting the magnitudes gets only 2.5 m/s.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Person: 0.5 m/s west; runner relative to person: 3.5 m/s east.
choices.rationale: Correct: East positive: v_person = +1.5 − 2.0 = −0.5 m/s. v_runner/person = 3.0 − (−0.5) = +3.5 m/s.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Person: 0.5 m/s east; runner relative to person: 2.5 m/s east.
choices.rationale: The person's walk of 2.0 m/s west is larger than the walkway's 1.5 m/s east, so the net motion is westward. The direction follows the larger velocity.

title: combine and subtract signed velocities in one dimension across two or three reference frames (variant 3)
stem: A river flows east at 3.0 m/s relative to the ground. A boat moves directly upstream, heading west, at 5.0 m/s relative to the water. A log floats freely with the current. Which choice gives the boat's velocity relative to the ground and the log's velocity relative to the boat?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Boat: 8.0 m/s west; log relative to boat: 11 m/s east.
choices.rationale: The current opposes the boat's westward motion since the boat heads upstream. The velocities subtract, giving 5.0 − 3.0 = 2.0 m/s.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Boat: 2.0 m/s west; log relative to boat: 5.0 m/s east.
choices.rationale: Correct: East positive: v_boat/ground = −5.0 + 3.0 = −2.0 m/s. v_log/boat = +3.0 − (−2.0) = +5.0 m/s. The log moves with the water, so v_log/boat equals the boat's speed through the water.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Boat: 2.0 m/s west; log relative to boat: 5.0 m/s west.
choices.rationale: The log drifts east relative to the ground while the boat moves west. From the boat, the log therefore moves east, not west.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Boat: 5.0 m/s west; log relative to boat: 8.0 m/s east.
choices.rationale: The boat's 5.0 m/s is measured relative to the water, not to the ground. The current has to be added in to find the ground velocity.

title: identify which quantities are invariant between frames moving at constant relative velocity (acceleration, time) and whi
stem: A train car moves east at a constant 20 m/s on straight, level track. A passenger tosses a ball straight up relative to the car, and it comes back to her hand. An observer on the ground watches the same flight. Which pair of quantities has the same value for both observers?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The ball's acceleration and its time of flight.
choices.rationale: Correct: Frames moving at constant relative velocity agree on acceleration (10 m/s² down) and elapsed time, but disagree on velocities, positions, and path shape.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The ball's speed at the highest point and its acceleration.
choices.rationale: At the top, the passenger sees zero speed, but the ground observer sees the ball still moving east at 20 m/s. The speeds differ even though the acceleration agrees.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The shape of the ball's path and its initial velocity.
choices.rationale: The passenger sees a straight vertical path, while the ground observer sees a parabola. The initial velocities also differ by the 20 m/s of the train.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The ball's velocity at release and its time of flight.
choices.rationale: The ground observer measures a horizontal component of 20 m/s that the passenger does not. The time of flight agrees, but the release velocity does not.

title: identify which quantities are invariant between frames moving at constant relative velocity (acceleration, time) and whi (variant 1)
stem: An elevator rises at a constant 3.0 m/s. A rider releases a coin from rest, relative to the elevator, and it falls to the floor. An observer outside the shaft watches the same event. Which pair of quantities has the same value for both observers?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The coin's initial velocity and its acceleration.
choices.rationale: The rider sees the coin start from rest, but the outside observer sees it start moving upward at 3.0 m/s. The initial velocities do not agree.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The coin's displacement and the time it takes to reach the floor.
choices.rationale: The elevator rises during the fall, so the outside observer sees a different displacement for the coin than the rider does.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The coin's acceleration and the time it takes to reach the floor.
choices.rationale: Correct: The elevator moves at constant velocity, so both frames measure a = 10 m/s² downward and the same fall time. Velocities and displacements differ by the elevator's 3.0 m/s.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The coin's speed when it reaches the floor and its acceleration.
choices.rationale: The speeds differ at impact because the observers measure velocity relative to different frames. Only the change in velocity is shared.

title: identify which quantities are invariant between frames moving at constant relative velocity (acceleration, time) and whi (variant 2)
stem: A boat moves at a constant 4.0 m/s east on calm water. A sailor throws a ball straight up relative to the boat, and she catches it at the same point on the deck. Someone on a stationary pier watches the flight. Which statement about the two observers' measurements is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They agree on the ball's horizontal velocity but disagree about its acceleration.
choices.rationale: The pier observer sees the ball move east at 4.0 m/s, while the sailor sees no horizontal motion. The acceleration is 10 m/s² downward for both.

choices.label: B
choices.text: They agree on the ball's acceleration and its flight time but disagree about its horizontal velocity.
choices.rationale: Correct: Constant relative velocity means the frames differ only by a constant velocity: a and t are shared, horizontal velocity (0 versus 4.0 m/s) is not.

choices.label: C
choices.text: They agree on the distance the ball travels but disagree about its flight time.
choices.rationale: The pier observer sees a longer, curved path, so the distance differs. The flight time is the same in both frames.

choices.label: D
choices.text: They agree on nothing about the ball's motion, since the frames are moving relative to each other.
choices.rationale: Frames moving at constant velocity relative to each other agree on accelerations and on elapsed time. Disagreement is limited to velocity and position values.

title: identify which quantities are invariant between frames moving at constant relative velocity (acceleration, time) and whi (variant 3)
stem: A cart rolls east at a constant 2.0 m/s along a lab bench. A spring in the cart launches a marble straight up, relative to the cart, and the marble lands back in the cart. A student at rest next to the bench also records the flight. Which choice lists quantities that are the same for both students?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The marble's acceleration and the time of flight.
choices.rationale: Correct: A cart moving at constant velocity is an inertial frame, so both students measure a = 10 m/s² and the same time. The horizontal velocity differs by 2.0 m/s.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The marble's acceleration and the horizontal distance it travels.
choices.rationale: The student at the bench sees the marble travel east with the cart, while the student riding the cart sees no horizontal travel. The distances differ.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The marble's speed at launch and the time of flight.
choices.rationale: The bench student sees a launch speed that combines the upward speed with the cart's 2.0 m/s. The launch speeds therefore differ.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The marble's speed at the top of its path and its acceleration.
choices.rationale: At the top, the cart student measures zero speed, while the bench student measures 2.0 m/s. The speeds differ.

title: resolve projectile velocity into independent horizontal (constant) and vertical (g-accelerated) components past the apex
stem: A ball is kicked from level ground with an initial horizontal velocity component of 12 m/s and an initial vertical component of 16 m/s. Neglecting air resistance, which choice gives the ball's speed and acceleration at t = 2.4 s, which is after it has passed its highest point?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Speed 8 m/s; acceleration 10 m/s² downward.
choices.rationale: The horizontal velocity component stays at 12 m/s, so it must be included. The speed is the magnitude of both components combined, not just the vertical one.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Speed about 14.4 m/s; acceleration 10 m/s² downward.
choices.rationale: Correct: The object peaks at t = 1.6 s. At t = 2.4 s, v_y = 16 − 10(2.4) = -8 m/s, v_x = 12 m/s, speed = sqrt(12² + -8²) = 14.4 m/s. The acceleration is 10 m/s² down all the way.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Speed 12 m/s; acceleration 10 m/s² downward.
choices.rationale: The horizontal component is constant, but the vertical component is now 8 m/s, which is not zero at this instant. The speed combines both.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Speed 20 m/s; acceleration 10 m/s² downward.
choices.rationale: Speed is the magnitude of the vector, found by combining perpendicular components with the Pythagorean theorem. Adding the components directly overestimates it.

title: resolve projectile velocity into independent horizontal (constant) and vertical (g-accelerated) components past the apex (variant 3)

title: compare range, time of flight, and maximum height for complementary launch angles at equal speed
stem: Two balls are launched from level ground at the same speed of 20 m/s, one at 30° and the other at 60° above the horizontal. Neglect air resistance and use g = 10 m/s². Which statement compares the flights correctly?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The 30° projectile lands farther away, because it has the larger horizontal velocity component.
choices.rationale: Horizontal speed alone does not set the range, since the time in the air matters too. Complementary angles give equal ranges because sin(2θ) is the same for both.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Both land about 35 m away and stay up for the same time, because they share a launch speed.
choices.rationale: The two projectiles have different vertical components, so they spend different times in the air. The one launched at the steeper angle stays up longer.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Both land about 35 m away; the 60° projectile stays up longer (3.5 s versus 2.0 s) and rises higher (15.0 m versus 5.0 m).
choices.rationale: Correct: R = v² sin(2θ)/g is equal for 30° and 60° (34.6 m). T = 2v sinθ/g gives 2.00 s and 3.46 s. H = (v sinθ)²/2g gives 5.00 m and 15.00 m.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The 60° projectile lands farther away, because it rises higher and stays up longer.
choices.rationale: A longer flight time is offset by a smaller horizontal velocity component. The two effects exactly cancel for complementary angles, giving the same range.

choices.text: The 55° projectile lands farther away, because it rises higher and stays up longer.
choices.rationale: A longer flight time is offset by a smaller horizontal velocity component. The two effects exactly cancel for complementary angles, giving the same range.
